newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CASH CRUDES HIT HARD BY GASOLINE, IRAQ RETURN.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CASH CRUDES HIT HARD BY GASOLINE, IRAQ RETURN.

text.p: U.S. crude prices were whacked twice on Friday, first by the collapse in gasoline values and later on news Iraq received final clearance from the U.N. bureacracy for selling oil again.

Traders in the U.S. Gulf said business was done at mostly weaker differentials, but activity slowed considerably once the morning ended. Most focus remained firmly on when Iraq would submit contracts to U.N. overseers, and subsequently land their exports.
U.S. companies Bayoil and Coastal were expected to load Iraqi crude in the next week to 10 days, depending on final arrangements with Iraq's State Oil and Marketing Organization (SOMO).
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ranged 55 cents lower by session's end, at $19.50-60 a barrel. September/October spreads remained around minus 20 cents.
NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures slid more than 2.00 cents a gallon to under 62.00 cents a gallon.
Deals left Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at a 11-16 cents premium to benchmark, selling lightly at plus 12 cents.
Other grades saw West Texas Sour/Midland sell at WTI/Cushing -$1.50 and Postings Plus between $1.85-87.
Steady price levels were seen for Midland/WTI at about 33 cents under WTI, traders said.
